tagline: Finds your data on broker sites, screenshots the evidence, and files the removals.
verdictSummary: The trackable part is real: a list of brokers, a record of which ones list you, a screenshot as proof, and a re-check on a schedule. What you cannot build is the removal itself. Optery submits opt-out requests on your behalf, which requires a signed authorisation, a support team handling the ones that need a phone call or an ID upload, and a legal footing to act as your agent. A personal build tells you where you are exposed; it cannot make it stop.
coreLoopDIY: Keep a local register of data brokers, capture a dated screenshot of any page that lists you, and get reminded to re-check each one on a cycle so a re-listing does not go unnoticed.
whatYouLose: removals submitted for you — you file every request yourself
the broker list, which runs to hundreds of sites and changes constantly
authorised-agent status, which is what makes some brokers respond at all
the support team that chases the ones which ignore the first request
whyPeopleStillPay: Because opting out is not hard, it is endless. Hundreds of brokers, each with its own form, each re-listing you a few months later, and the entire value of the subscription is that somebody else does it every month forever.
notes: Upstream's draft for this entry carried a password-manager prompt (Argon2id, encrypted vault, master key) that has nothing to do with a data-broker service; rewritten from the actual product. The prompt deliberately never submits anything on the user's behalf.
prompt:
Build a personal data-exposure register: a local tool that tracks where your personal information appears on data-broker sites and whether it has come back.

Data model: a broker record holds a name, the URL of its opt-out page, the method it accepts (web form, email, postal), a typical response time, and free-text notes on the process. Ship an empty database and a documented import format rather than a bundled list, since any list shipped today is wrong within months.

Exposure records: for each broker, the user records whether they were found, what was exposed (name, address, phone, relatives, employer), and the URL of the listing. A capture action opens the listing URL in a headless browser, saves a full-page screenshot and the raw HTML into a dated folder, and links them to the record. That evidence archive is the point of the tool: it is what you attach to a follow-up when a broker claims it never listed you.

Removal workflow: mark a broker as requested, with the date and the method used. Generate a removal request from a template the user edits, including their reference details, and copy it to the clipboard or open a pre-filled mail draft. The tool must never submit a form, log into a site, or send an email on the user's behalf — automating that means impersonating them against sites that never agreed to it, and a bounced automated request is worse than a slow manual one. State this as a design decision in the README.

Re-check cycle: each broker carries a re-check interval, defaulting to 90 days. The dashboard shows what is due, what is overdue, and which brokers have re-listed after a previous successful removal, which is the single most useful number this tool produces.

Reporting: a timeline per broker and an export of the whole register as CSV plus the evidence folder.

Out of scope: automated submission, credential storage, any hosted service, and scanning the web for exposures the user has not found themselves.

faq.q: Can I import Optery's list of brokers it covers?
faq.a: Optery publishes the broker names it covers, so a list can be assembled by hand, but there is no export that includes the opt-out URLs and methods in a usable form. Building the register is genuinely the work here, and it is the part that stays useful after you cancel.

faq.q: How is this different from just keeping a spreadsheet?
faq.a: The screenshot capture and the re-check scheduling. A spreadsheet does not prove a broker listed you in March, and it does not tell you in June that the same broker is listing you again. Both of those are what makes an opt-out campaign stick.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing but disk. It runs locally, the headless browser is free, and the screenshots are the only thing that grows. A few hundred captures is a few hundred megabytes.

faq.q: What is the one thing that does not survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Somebody else doing it. Optery's entire value is that removals happen without you, month after month, including the brokers that require a phone call. This build hands you a well-organised to-do list, which is honest but is not the same product.
